---
title: Bring your own model
description: Load your own network for segmentation or inference, pin it by digest, and read its tensors back.
---

You're not stuck with our models. Segmentation, inference and the trackers all
take bytes you hand them, so something you trained, quantised and shipped in
your own bundle runs on exactly the same path the built-in ones do.

## Loading a model

`enable_segmentation` takes the model itself, not a path to one we know about.
The bytes are yours, and so is deciding how they get versioned and updated.

```c
goss_status status = goss_session_enable_segmentation(
    session,
    model_bytes,   /* your network, as loaded from your bundle */
    model_len,
    4              /* worker threads; 0 lets the engine choose */
);
```

The thread count is the one knob worth setting yourself. It caps the inference
worker, and it's usually what decides whether a model fits in the frame budget
or not.

<Note>
Like everything else on a session, this has to happen on the graph thread. Turn
the worker on before you start submitting frames, not partway through.
</Note>

## Checking a model will run before you ship it

Each build has a set of operations compiled into it. If your network uses one
that isn't there, it fails when you enable it, which is a terrible moment to
find out.

`goss_ml_op_support` lets you ask ahead of time:

```c
uint8_t report[4096];
size_t written = 0;
goss_ml_op_support(model_bytes, model_len, report, sizeof report, &written);
```

The report lists the operations your model wants and which of them this build
can run. Put it in CI against every model you ship and the library version you
ship with, and no user will ever be the one who finds the problem.

## Pinning models by digest

A model is executable content. If your app downloads models, or loads them from
a directory the user can write to, then whatever can write to that directory
gets to choose what your camera runs.

The allowlist closes that off. Give the session the SHA-256 digests you trust,
and anything whose digest isn't on the list gets refused when you enable a
tracker or segmenter.

```c
/* 32 bytes, raw, not hex. */
goss_session_allow_model_digest(session, digest_of_my_segmenter);
goss_session_allow_model_digest(session, digest_of_my_detector);
```

A few things to know:

- Call it **before** you enable the worker, because that's when the check
  happens.
- Adding the same digest twice does nothing, so you can call it on every
  startup without keeping track.
- If you set no digests, anything loads. That's the default, and it's the right
  one while you're developing.
- `goss_session_clear_model_allowlist` empties the list again.

<Warning>
An empty allowlist means "allow everything", not "allow nothing". If your app
can download models, set the list explicitly at startup. Don't assume the empty
state is the locked one.
</Warning>

## Reading your model's output

There are two calls, and which you want depends on what your model produces.

**Plain numbers.** `ml_output` copies one node's output tensor into memory you
own.

```c
float values[1024];
size_t written = 0;
goss_session_ml_output(session,
                       node_id, node_id_len,  /* which ml.infer node */
                       0,                     /* which output tensor */
                       values, 1024, &written);
```

**A mask.** `ml_mask` copies a node's mask-bound output, freshly read and
resampled onto the fixed segmentation plane, so it lines up with everything
else from that frame.

```c
float mask[256 * 256];
size_t written = 0;
goss_session_ml_mask(session, node_id, node_id_len, mask, 256 * 256, &written);
```

Both write into your buffer, so allocate once and reuse it. Allocating here
means allocating in the hot path.

Both tell you how much they wrote. Check that instead of assuming the shape,
and size the buffer from the model you shipped rather than from a number you
typed once.

## Wiring a model into a lens

Your model becomes part of what draws when a lens references it as an
`ml.infer` node. The node id you pass to `ml_output` and `ml_mask` is the one
the manifest gave it, which is how a lens author and an app agree on what to
read without sharing a header. See [the lens format](/docs/concepts/lenses).

## Turning it off

`goss_session_disable_segmentation` stops the worker and gives back what it was
holding. Do that when the feature leaves the screen, not when the session ends,
so somebody who closed the camera isn't still paying for a model.

## Before you ship

- `goss_ml_op_support` passes against the library version you're shipping with.
- You've measured the thread count rather than guessed it.
- Digests are pinned if models can arrive from anywhere other than your binary.
- Output buffers get allocated once, sized from the model.
- The worker is off when the feature isn't on screen.
